text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: SEV3: elevated 5xx from model-runner fleet in us-west-2. Metrics show spike in 502/504 starting ~1754242400. Alert group: runtime-errors.

alice_oncall: on it — pinging SRE and infra. Do we have a pager? who grabbed?

ben_sre: I picked this up. Seeing repeated SIGSEGV on runner-003 and OOM kills on runner-007.

ben_sre: snippet from dmesg on runner-003:
```
[12345.678901] Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (model_runner) score 987 or sacrifice child
[12345.679012] model_runner(4123): segfault at 0 ip 0x7f3a2c4a sp 0x7ffdc9e8 error 4 in libattention.so[7f3a2c000+20000]
```

dave_infra: confirmed. Node-level OOM + kernel oom_killer invoked on a couple hosts. Memory pressure correlates with long sequences from a customer batch.

carla_support: customer-impact: three customers (acct ids ending 77/82/91) reported 502s and timeouts in last 5m. One has a production traffic spike.

eline_custops: please escalate customer 77 — they're in a closed beta, high priority. I'll open a bridge if we need to brief them.

alice_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) mark affected hosts drain-only; 2) ramp fallback routing to smaller model variant and Dedicated pool; 3) reduce default batch_size env to 1 for new runners; 4) restart model-runner with safer flags; 5) collect kcore and traces. Who can run the drain?

ben_sre: running drain now on runner-003/007/011. Command: `kubectl annotate node runner-003 redwood/drain=incident-1754242424 && kubectl cordon runner-003`

dave_infra: opening autoscale to add 6 warm spare instances in us-west-2, and enabling immediate burst capacity. Also applying `RLIMIT_AS=4g` temporary cap to reduce blast radius on restarts.

ben_sre: temp rollback: switching traffic from model-v2-quant to model-v2-128q on the gateway rule. Patch: `PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id} {"model":"model-v2-128q","traffic_percent":100}`

carla_support: notified affected customers via status page and direct messages: customer 77 is on the bridge now.

alice_oncall: collect heap profiles and KVCache size from the problematic runs before restart. ben — can you capture `gcore` and upload to /tmp/incident-1754242424/ ?

ben_sre: grabbing gcore; if process is gone we'll pull last core. Also saving /var/log/model_runner/*.log and tracer snapshots.

ben_sre: quick hotpatch idea: set `MAX_SEQ_LEN=1024` and `BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=20` to reduce memory per-request. Will push to canary group after drain.

dave_infra: pushed env changes to canary (3 nodes) and started a rolling restart. Canary shows no OOMs for 6 minutes but still a small increase in 5xx from adapters during restart.

incidents-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied: traffic shifted (model-v2-128q), 6 warm spares added, drain executed on 4 nodes. Error rate down from 18% to 2.1% in last 10 minutes.

carla_support: customers 82/91 reporting recovery. Customer 77 still sees intermittent errors but latency improved.

alice_oncall: good. Next steps: 1) keep fallback routing for 30m; 2) collect artifacts for postmortem; 3) schedule hotfix to fix KV cache growth during long sequences; 4) assign owners for follow-up.

ben_sre: artifacts saved to s3://redwood-incidents/1754242424/{gcore,logs,profiles}. I will open a blameless postmortem ticket and assign root cause triage.

dave_infra: I'll keep autoscale + warm spares for 1h and then scale down.

eline_custops: I'll send customer 77 a status update and offer a meeting if needed.

alice_oncall: thanks team. Closing incident channel in 15m unless errors resurge. Assigning follow-ups: ben_sre (root cause), dave_infra (capacity and env safeguards), carla_support (customer comms).

ben_sre: :thumbsup: initial hypothesis: a memory leak triggered by long-sequence KV cache growth interacting with quantized attention kernel — reproducing locally. Will dump more traces.

incidents-bot: :hourglass_flowing_sand: update scheduled in 10m.

alice_oncall: marking this thread resolved for now — setting status to degraded -> recovered once metrics hold. Postmortem ETA EOD.

carla_support: closing bridge for customer 77 — will reopen if they see further issues.

ben_sre: follow-up note: avoid `BATCH_SIZE>8` for this model until we patch; will push a recommended config to docs.

incidents-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved (mitigated).
